receive_window.derivation: R=alpha_max+xi_nu=2 and S=2*N*c1=5 from the fixed AFDM design. Union the bins -S*l-R through -S*l+R modulo 256 for all l=0,...,5, giving -27,...,2 modulo 256.
receive_window.resource_note: These are received pilot-response samples, not new transmitted pilots. The selected 64 active pilots, 4032 guard cells and 4096 useful pilot-energy budget remain unchanged.
receive_window.limitation: Fractional Doppler has nonzero tails outside this finite receive region and permits residual data leakage. Taking all 64 transmitted non-data positions as received pilot observations incorrectly includes directly shifted data even in static A.

processing_window.rule: Estimate one frame-reference delay/Doppler/gain set jointly from all 64 pilot-bearing blocks, then evaluate each block's channel using the continuous CP-inclusive clock. Do not pool independent frames.
processing_window.scope: Same observation time as OFDM; the transmitter remains 64 separate 256-sample AFDM blocks. This does not select a frame-wide DAFT or data-equalizer matrix.

design.clock_and_gain_reference: The native unit pilot template uses gain at the first useful receive sample. Define g_ref at the first transmitted CP sample, t=0; then g_p,b=g_p,ref*exp(+j*2*pi*f_p*((N+CP)*b+CP)/Fs). Do not average complex block gains without this phase evolution.

search_parameters.initial_grid_rule: Use symmetric multiples of 1/(4*T_frame), include zero and both fixed support endpoints. Keep this grid fixed across A/B, Eb/N0 and realizations; never insert actual path frequencies.
search_parameters.refinement_rule: Bounded golden-section refinement around the selected coarse candidate, retaining the coarse point and support endpoints. Stop when the remaining bracket is at most 1 Hz; this is numerical precision, not a 1-Hz estimation-accuracy guarantee.
search_parameters.initialization_and_stopping: Start with the received pilot observations as residual. Add one candidate path at each of the P=3 steps and refit all selected gains by joint LS after each addition. Stop after three paths; no extra outer iterations or data-decision feedback.
search_parameters.candidate_score: Squared residual correlation divided by the candidate atom energy orthogonal to already selected atoms. This is the conditional LS objective improvement for fixed previous path parameters.
search_parameters.scope: Sequential approximation to the nonlinear joint ML search, adapted to our selected 64-block window. It is not an exhaustive global-ML solution or a claim of exact replication of the source's per-block search. Same-delay paths with distinct Dopplers are allowed; only numerical linear dependence is rejected.

design.source_condition: The source's fractional approximate-ML derivation uses weak inter-path template overlap and reports good performance for distinct path delays. The selected generator has distinct delays, but no extra receiver oracle or distinct-delay search constraint is adopted.
reference_sections: VI, equations (67)-(71): pilot observation model and joint gain estimation
design.reference_scope: One source AFDM frame is one of our 256-sample blocks. Our joint 64-block window and sequential numerical search are explicitly selected adaptations of the pilot-template approximate-ML/LS principle.
design.support_implementation: afdm.py: native transforms and fractional-Doppler pilot response; afdm_estimation.py: joint observations, sequential path search, conditional LS gains and frame-reference tap reconstruction

implementation_diagnostic.scope: 16 paired diagnostic frames for each A/B condition, with no AWGN and each existing 0:5:30-dB Eb/N0 point. True path parameters and noise variance are not passed to the actual estimator. Known-hypothesis, alternate-delay and same-delay cases are separate algebraic controls.
implementation_diagnostic.findings: The joint observation matrix matches an independent serial pilot channel to below 3.22e-14 relative error in the controls. Search uses a fixed 1920-by-642 dictionary, three sequential path additions and local refinement intervals below 1 Hz. All diagnostic estimates are finite, rank 3 and within the common support; known physical-profile delay multisets were recovered in these 16-frame cases. These are implementation checks, not BER or universal accuracy claims.
implementation_diagnostic.preserved_limits: No condition-specific tuning, perfect path information, data-feedback cancellation or renormalization is added. Residual estimator errors remain part of the future receiver comparison.

structural_diagnostic.scope: Transform/pilot-template validation and received-window data-leakage probes; no path estimator, noise study, equalizer or BER run.
structural_diagnostic.findings: Native pilot response agrees with an independent serial channel to about 1.40e-13 relative error. The proposed window is isolated from data in static A to numerical precision; B-4 retains nonzero leakage. This validates the observation construction, not estimation accuracy or BER superiority.

pending_design: data covariance, residual/noise policy, MMSE solving and complete BER implementation; the selected block scope and estimated DAFT/data operators are implemented under receiver_equalization_policy

design.decision_record: The user accepted fitting the entire fractional-Doppler DD pilot response, joint-LS path gains and the agreed DD linear-MMSE flow, using all 64 slots and the same quarter-frame-bin coarse grid and 1-Hz local refinement as AFDM. The existing native mask and pilot energy are preserved.
receiver_flow: remove the per-slot CP and apply the native OTFS basis demodulation
extract all Doppler bins at the possible pilot-arrival delay rows
fit P=3 integer-delay and continuous-Doppler pilot templates by sequential approximate ML
refit all selected complex gains jointly by LS after each path addition
reconstruct the channel from estimated parameters for the agreed DD linear-MMSE data receiver
design.known_information: Only the common P=3, integer excess-delay support 0..5, fixed +/-46875-Hz residual Doppler bound, frame design and known DD pilot. True active delays, per-path Dopplers, gains, unknown data and current A/B level are unavailable.

receive_window.derivation: The native ISFFT-plus-OFDM useful time grid equals a unitary IFFT along Doppler. A pilot at delay 128 occupies within-slot sample 128; any allowed integer delay l=0..5 moves its response to DD delay row 128+l. Fractional Doppler spreads over all 64 Doppler bins, which are retained.
receive_window.resource_note: Received observations only, not additional transmitted pilots. The single 64+0j pilot, 4095 guard/reserved cells, 12288 data cells and 4096 useful transmit pilot-energy budget are unchanged.
receive_window.validity_scope: Current rectangular native transform, aligned per-slot CP=5 and integer excess delays without pilot delay-row wrap. The existing non-data rows isolate this observation region from data for every allowed delay. Fractional delays, timing/filter effects or a changed layout require review.

processing_window.rule: Estimate one frame-reference delay/Doppler/gain set from the complete 64-slot DD response. Use the CP-inclusive receive clock and do not pool independent frames. This selects estimation scope, not the data-equalizer matrix dimensions.

design.pilot_observation_equation: For path (l,f), put FFT_b[(64/sqrt(64))*exp(j*2*pi*32*b/64)*exp(j*2*pi*f*((256+5)*b+5+128+l)/Fs)] with unitary FFT in DD delay row 128+l and zero in the other observed delay rows. Sum these columns times their jointly fitted complex gains, plus receiver noise.
design.clock_and_gain_reference: Complex path gain is defined at the frame's first transmitted CP sample t=0. The pilot-arrival clock includes CP and the within-slot arrival sample 128+l. Do not replace it with the useful-only frame clock or round Doppler to a DD bin.

search_parameters.initial_grid_rule: Same fixed symmetric quarter-frame-bin grid as AFDM, with zero and both support endpoints: 107 frequencies times 6 delays = 642 candidates. Do not insert true path frequencies or adapt to an A/B condition.
search_parameters.refinement_rule: Bounded golden-section refinement around a selected coarse point, retaining evaluated coarse/support points. Stop at a remaining bracket of at most 1 Hz. This is numerical precision, not guaranteed estimation accuracy.
search_parameters.initialization_and_stopping: Start from received pilot observations, add one path per step, jointly refit every selected gain and stop after P=3 additions. No extra outer iterations or data-decision feedback.
search_parameters.candidate_score: Squared residual correlation divided by candidate atom energy orthogonal to already selected atoms; conditional joint-LS objective improvement with previous path parameters fixed.
search_parameters.scope: Sequential approximation to joint nonlinear ML, not an exhaustive global-ML solution. Permit same-delay paths with distinct Dopplers; reject numerical linear dependence rather than imposing the generator's distinct active delays.

design.estimation_interpretation: The full fractional-Doppler pilot template is exact for this selected isolated integer-delay model. The three-step nonlinear search is approximate and does not guarantee global ML, full parameter recovery or a BER ranking. Do not treat the three largest DD cells as three physical paths.
design.reference_scope: The reference motivates the embedded DD pilot, fractional-Doppler spreading and full-Doppler guard, but uses threshold-based channel estimation and message-passing detection. Our continuous path-template approximate-ML/joint-LS estimator and DD linear-MMSE detector family are explicit project choices, not that paper's original algorithm.
design.support_implementation: otfs.py: native transforms and per-slot CP; otfs_estimation.py: DD pilot observations, exact native templates, conditional joint LS and frame-reference tap reconstruction; pilot_path_search.py: shared sequential search also used by AFDM

implementation_diagnostic.scope: 16 paired diagnostic frames per A/B condition, with no AWGN and each existing 0:5:30-dB point: 640 inputs in total. Actual searches receive public settings and received samples only; known-hypothesis, alternate-delay, same-delay and support-endpoint cases are separate mathematical controls.
implementation_diagnostic.findings: Across 78 single-path probes, native templates match the independent serial channel to below 1.02e-14 relative error and data-only leakage in the receive region is below 9.64e-17 relative to the pilot L2 norm. All 640 actual-profile estimates are finite, in bounds and rank 3, with nonincreasing joint-LS residuals and final local intervals below 1 Hz. The true delay multisets were recovered in this small diagnostic, not proven universally recoverable.
implementation_diagnostic.preserved_limits: No global-ML or BER superiority claim, condition-specific tuning, true-data cancellation, oracle path parameters or gain renormalization. Remaining estimator errors are retained for later equalization and BER. Data-channel matrices and the full DD-MMSE receiver remain pending.

pending_design: data covariance, residual/noise policy, numerical MMSE solver, bit detection and complete BER implementation; the selected full-frame DD/data operator is implemented under receiver_equalization_policy

receiver_equalization_policy.existing_DD_a_design: Preserve the selected DD-ML alternating-projection estimator and ICI-aware 256-by-256 TF linear-MMSE matrix for each of 64 symbols. The new common-family choice does not replace that design.
receiver_equalization_policy.development_focus: The user clarified that the target is BER comparison, not eliminating all channel-estimation errors or repeatedly optimizing OFDM. Keep the current OFDM BEM-LS prototype as an initial candidate with documented limits, distinguish implementation errors from estimator limitations, and specify the other receivers under the agreed common conditions.
pending_design: retain the fixed OFDM BEM-LS initial candidate and documented limitations alongside the other implemented estimators/solvers
full frame/bit accounting, confidence intervals and BER implementation and validation
receiver_equalization_policy.baseline_scope: The initial single-path LOS plus AWGN validation and its perfect common-frequency correction remain unchanged. This policy does not grant perfect multipath channel knowledge.
receiver_equalization_policy.reference_basis: Section V-D uses ICI-aware MMSE equalizers for the OFDM/DD-a-OFDM comparison. Extending the linear-MMSE family to all four native receivers is our agreed experimental choice; it does not require copying a source paper's estimator or detector for every waveform.
receiver_equalization_policy.other_equalizer_families: Not selected for the initial comparison. This status means an experimental choice is pending or excluded, not that other receiver methodologies do not exist in the literature.

receiver_information_policy.availability_rule: Make P=3 available equally to all four receivers. A receiver may use this prior when its algorithm supports it; this does not require every receiver to use a path-parametric estimator.

delay_support.reference: Excess delay relative to the aligned LOS receive window, at 60 MHz; not the absolute satellite-to-ground propagation time.
delay_support.availability_rule: Provide the same 0..5-sample support bound to all four receivers. Integer-delay candidates are 0,1,2,3,4,5; the actual active locations 0,2,5 are not supplied.
delay_support.basis: Use the already selected maximum excess delay and CP length. Fractional-delay modeling and any wider timing uncertainty require a separate review.

residual_doppler_support.scope: All four receivers in the first three-path A/B comparison, after perfect common LOS correction.
residual_doppler_support.availability_rule: Provide the same fixed maximum support to all four receivers. Do not provide a current sweep level's magnitude or any path's actual Doppler. Receiver algorithms may use this common bound according to their selected design.
residual_doppler_support.baseline_scope: No change to common LOS correction or generated path Dopplers. A wider or erroneous design support is a separate extension.

receiver_information_policy.parameter_estimation_rule: Obtain the channel response or path parameters from the agreed pilot observations. Do not copy the actual 0/2/5-sample delays, per-path Dopplers, or complex gains from the channel generator into the receivers.
receiver_information_policy.purpose: First compare channel-parameter estimation and BER without adding path-count detection errors. State this known-count assumption in reported results; equal path-count information alone does not settle other fairness conditions.
receiver_information_policy.baseline_scope: This policy does not change the initial single-path LOS AWGN baseline or its perfect common-Doppler knowledge and compensation. Future multipath compensation details remain to be discussed.
receiver_information_policy.remaining_receiver_design: All receivers share P=3, 0..5-sample excess-delay bounds and fixed +/-46875-Hz residual Doppler support; true active path parameters remain unavailable. Native pilot/channel/data operators, separate silent noise measurement and Es=1 MMSE symbol solves are implemented and initially diagnosed, including direct/full-DD CG and zero-noise SVD/LSQR. Standard estimated-gain-aware Gray hard bit decisions are now implemented under data_bit_recovery. Full frame/bit accounting and four-way BER remain pending. Nonzero estimation error alone does not require redesign.

path_count_estimation_followup.purpose: Replace the known count with a receiver-estimated count and compare against the known-count reference. Assess missed or spurious paths and their impact on parameter estimation and BER.
path_count_estimation_followup.comparison_rule: Review the receiver-information and resource conditions for all four schemes before this extension; no scheme receives the true count as hidden assistance in an estimated-count comparison.

pilot_comparison_policy.fairness_interpretation: Compare four pilot-based transceiver designs under matched non-data resource and total useful-signal pilot-energy budgets. Native pilots and channel estimators can differ. All four use estimated-channel pilot subtraction and data-only unknowns with full native receive observations, within the selected local TF/DAFT or frame-wide OTFS DD scope. Data covariance, noise policy and numerical MMSE solving remain pending. BER differences include those design effects; do not attribute all differences to intrinsic modulation-waveform behavior alone.
pilot_comparison_policy.pilot_plus_pilot_guard_resource_fraction: Use the same fraction of the frame's resources for pilots and pilot-specific guard or reserved cells across all four schemes.
pilot_comparison_policy.total_pilot_energy_rule: Match the total energy allocated to pilot signals across all four schemes; do not treat a higher-power pilot as free.
pilot_comparison_policy.total_pilot_energy_units: Normalized transmit energy per useful frame before the channel, with the existing average data-symbol energy E_s=1; excludes CP/CPP energy and is not power in watts.

initial_budget.budget_unit: One common 256-by-64 useful grid, with 16384 native complex-symbol degrees of freedom. Count the union of pilot and pilot-specific guard/reserved cells; count CP/CPP samples and energy separately.

energy_budget.allocation_rule: Uniform energy per active pilot within each scheme: |x_p|^2 = E_p/N_p. OFDM/DD-a-OFDM use energy 1, AFDM uses 64 and OTFS uses 4096 per active cell, all in E_s units. Match total pilot energy across schemes; do not rescale data or individual frames.
energy_budget.note: Normalized simulation energy, not watts. Known phases are fixed in known_pilot_sequence. OFDM/DD-a-OFDM have 4096 pilots of magnitude 1, AFDM has 64 of magnitude 8, and OTFS has one 64+0j pilot. Data remain uncoded Gray 16-QAM with E_s=1. Equality applies to useful transmit energy before the channel and CP; copied-prefix energy is recorded separately and is not automatically equal.

initial_budget.ofdm_and_dd_a_rule: Use identical TF pilot positions, known pilot values, and pilot energy distribution for the OFDM/DD-a-OFDM pair.
initial_budget.native_layout_rule: AFDM uses DAFT-domain pilot/guard placement and OTFS uses DD-domain placement. Design each actual mask within the common non-data budget; do not force identical coordinates across different bases.
initial_budget.reporting_rule: Record each scheme's nonzero pilot count, pilot-specific guard/reserved count, data count, and total pilot energy separately, in addition to the common combined overhead fraction.

conditional_afdm_budget_screen.layout_assumption: One embedded pilot in each 256-point AFDM block is now selected; the agreed mask expands the cited 59-cell pilot-plus-guard count to 64 cells by adding five zero guards per block.
conditional_afdm_budget_screen.note: A conditional resource count, not a universal minimum or a leakage-free guarantee. It uses the current AFDM design bounds and margin; full fractional-Doppler leakage and receiver performance still require validation. Different pilot layouts or Doppler support can change the budget.

initial_budget.selection_basis: The agreed initial 25-percent budget is a convenient rounding above the conditional 59/256 AFDM count. It is not an optimized ratio or a demonstrated minimum for all four schemes; uniform per-block allocation is not imposed by this frame-level budget.
remaining_checks: check pilot-data leakage, identifiability and estimation accuracy for all four native layouts using the selected fixed pilot values
measure CP energy under the agreed prefix_policy and account for full-frame energy costs
preserve the agreed information-bit quota when framing data and padding

known_pilot_sequence.hash_encoding: SHA256 of the 4096 integer phase indices converted to uint8 bytes, in sequence order.
known_pilot_sequence.OFDM_and_DD_a_OFDM: Use identical full master phase sequences, each multiplied by magnitude 1.
known_pilot_sequence.AFDM: Use the first 64 entries of the same master phase sequence, each multiplied by magnitude 8, in block order.
known_pilot_sequence.OTFS: Single known pilot 64+0j, with phase zero.
known_pilot_sequence.reuse_rule: Generate deterministically from a dedicated local RNG. Reuse the same values across frames, independent BER trials, Eb/N0 points, A/B Doppler levels and orbit snapshots; do not draw from data-bit or random channel-phase streams.
known_pilot_sequence.receiver_knowledge: All transmitted pilot values are known a priori at their corresponding receivers. This does not reveal unknown channel delays, differential Dopplers or complex path gains.
known_pilot_sequence.selection_basis: Reproducible initial constant-modulus pilot choice; not a validated optimum or a paper-mandated sequence. Data modulation remains 16-QAM.

shared_ofdm_dd_a_tf_layout.index_origin_convention: Use zero-based array coordinates and place the first pilot at (frequency=0, time=0); this fixes a reproducible grid origin for the agreed spacing.
shared_ofdm_dd_a_tf_layout.pilot_index_rule: Pilot at (m,n) iff m % 2 == 0 and n % 2 == 0, for 0 <= m < 256 and 0 <= n < 64. All remaining TF cells carry data.
shared_ofdm_dd_a_tf_layout.paired_rule: Use exactly the same mask, known pilot values and energy allocation for OFDM and DD-a-OFDM. Keep this layout fixed across A and all B levels; the separately agreed AFDM/OTFS native-domain masks use the same overhead and total pilot energy budgets.
shared_ofdm_dd_a_tf_layout.energy_note: Every active pilot has energy 1, with fixed QPSK phases and identical values for OFDM/DD-a-OFDM. Total useful-signal pilot energy is 4096; CP energy remains separate.

basic_sampling_screen.interpretation: The uniform TF sample model's basic delay period is 1/(d_f*Delta_f), and symmetric Doppler alias bound is 1/(2*d_t*T_block), with CP included in T_block. The agreed delay profile and residual Doppler envelope fit these basic ranges; this is not a proof of fractional-Doppler leakage suppression, path identifiability or BER performance.

afdm_daft_layout.placement_note: Zero-based cyclic DAFT coordinates: one pilot at zero, with 31 zero guards before it and 32 after it. Repeat in all 64 blocks and all A/B conditions.
afdm_daft_layout.validation_note: The 64-cell non-data mask contains the cited 59-cell mask under the agreed c1/margin bounds. Fractional-Doppler tails remain present; this is not a leakage-free or BER guarantee.

otfs_dd_layout.placement_note: Place one pilot at the DD-grid center. Reserve 64 delay rows across all 64 Doppler columns; all cells in this region except the pilot are zero. Keep the same mask for A and every B level.
otfs_dd_layout.resource_note: The 704-cell full-Doppler guard region includes the pilot. The other 3392 cells are extra zero reservations to match the agreed 25-percent comparison budget, not a claimed minimum guard requirement.
otfs_dd_layout.validation_note: The full-Doppler guard construction is a starting layout for the agreed integer excess delays and per-slot CP. Validate with the exact native channel; no complete estimator, equalizer or BER result is implied.

validation.scope: Use the agreed fixed pilots and uniform energy split. Check repeatability, shared basic phase values, isolated-pilot useful-signal energy before CP and native-grid roundtrips. The OTFS data-only guard diagnostic uses aligned integer delays 0/2/5 and every agreed residual Doppler level; it is not a channel estimator or BER test. AFDM fractional-Doppler estimation leakage remains pending.

pilot_comparison_policy.note: Native masks, known pilot values and uniform per-scheme pilot energy allocation are implemented. build_grid uses the selected fixed pilots by default and still accepts explicitly supplied values for controlled diagnostics, without rescaling them. Keep 25-percent non-data resources and 4096-E_s useful-signal pilot energy. CP energy remains separate. No completed channel estimator or four-way BER simulation is supplied here.

baseline.purpose: First validate the four transceivers and their energy/noise normalization in a single-path LOS plus complex AWGN channel with perfectly known and fully corrected common Doppler; this stage does not test Doppler robustness.

multipath_followup.profile_basis: Agreed synthetic, LOS-dominant three-path comparison condition; not a measurement of the SKKU–STARLINK-5285 channel or a standardized NTN profile.
multipath_followup.doppler_model: Apply the orbit-derived LOS Doppler at each snapshot to all three paths, with zero additional per-path Doppler as a first approximation for a fixed ground station and stationary local reflectors. This does not model differential Doppler spread.

doppler_effect_followup.purpose: After single-path baseline validation, compare the agreed three-path delay profile with zero residual Doppler (A) against the same profile with progressively larger differential path Doppler (B).
doppler_effect_followup.per_path_doppler_model: Controlled synthetic differential-Doppler sweep, not measured or geometry-derived SKKU reflection Doppler. At each agreed maximum residual magnitude d, use [0, +d, -d] in the fixed path order [los, reflection_1, reflection_2]. The sign assignment is the same across levels and all four schemes.

sweep_magnitude_design.definition: d = max_p(abs(delta_f_p)), where delta_f_p is each path's residual Doppler after perfect common LOS correction; delta_f_LOS = 0. This is a maximum magnitude relative to LOS, not the full signed Doppler spread max(delta_f_p)-min(delta_f_p).
sweep_magnitude_design.interpretation: Five exploratory conditions total: zero Doppler is A, and the four positive maximum magnitudes define B-1 through B-4. Levels are an agreed synthetic sensitivity-study choice, not measured Starlink differential Doppler or a standard-mandated grid.
sweep_magnitude_design.sampling_note: Preserve the physical Doppler frequencies without rounding to integer DD bins. Re-evaluate the normalization explicitly if the common subcarrier spacing changes.

common_doppler_compensation_policy.common_doppler_source: Orbit-derived LOS shift at the selected snapshot, shared by all paths before their additional offsets.
common_doppler_compensation_policy.receiver_knowledge: Provide the exact common LOS frequency for correction before waveform-specific demodulation. Do not provide the additional reflection-path Dopplers, delays, or complex gains; the agreed P=3 prior remains available to all four receivers.
common_doppler_compensation_policy.correction: Apply exp(-j*2*pi*f_LOS*n/F_s) after channel summation and receiver AWGN, with a continuous sample time including the per-block prefixes.
common_doppler_compensation_policy.per_path_residual_after_correction: additional_doppler_hz_to_los; it is zero on LOS in both A and B.

signed_reflection_doppler_pattern.path_binding: reflection_1 retains excess delay 2 samples and relative power -10 dB; reflection_2 retains excess delay 5 samples and relative power -15 dB. Do not swap the Doppler signs between paths or trials.

paired_conditions.comparison_control: At each Eb/N0, reuse a trial's path magnitudes and initial phases across A, B sweep levels, and all four schemes. Only the selected differential Doppler changes. Keep a fixed finalized pilot design and receiver settings across the sweep unless an explicitly agreed common adaptation rule is introduced.
paired_conditions.snapshot_interpretation: If the residual profile is the same, perfect common correction makes peak and exit equivalent residual-Doppler conditions. The synthetic B levels, rather than the raw orbit shifts, define the Doppler stress.

doppler_effect_followup.within_frame_evolution: Initial phases and path magnitudes stay fixed per trial; B adds deterministic exp(j*2*pi*delta_f_p*t) path phase rotation with continuous time including prefixes. No additional random phase or amplitude evolution is selected.
pending_design: Pilot-mask feasibility and receiver estimation search support for the agreed residual envelope
doppler_effect_followup.note: The existing explicit zero-additional-Doppler profile supplies A. B overrides only its path Dopplers using the agreed signed vectors above; delays, powers, normalization and paired initial phases remain unchanged. These are selected settings, not an implemented channel generator or BER results. Imperfect common correction is a separate unselected extension.

path_phase_and_gain_realization.path_magnitudes: Fixed at the agreed relative powers throughout each frame; no within-frame amplitude fading in the first comparison.
path_phase_and_gain_realization.relative_phases: Draw a new random initial reflection-path phase combination for each independent BER trial and keep these initial-phase parameters fixed within that trial; deterministic common and condition-B differential Doppler rotations are applied separately.

phase_distribution.reflection_phases_rad: Independent continuous uniform draws on [0, 2*pi) for each BER trial.

path_phase_and_gain_realization.paired_comparison: Reuse the same initial relative-phase realization for OFDM, AFDM, OTFS, and DD-a-OFDM, the low/high snapshots, and the paired A/B sweep levels within a trial.
path_phase_and_gain_realization.within_frame_time_variation: The explicit zero-additional-Doppler profile retains only common orbit-derived phase rotation. Condition B additionally uses deterministic differential-Doppler phase rotation as defined in doppler_effect_followup; no random amplitude or phase evolution is added.

power_normalization.common_complex_gain_scale: 1/sqrt(sum_p(P_p)); apply once to all path gains so sum_p(|h_p|^2) = 1 while preserving the agreed relative powers.
power_normalization.scope: Channel-profile level, not a per-frame or per-frequency-bin received-power adjustment.
power_normalization.receiver_noise: The data-symbol-reference AWGN variance, conditional unitary-transform sample rule, and initial 60 MHz sample grid are defined separately. Any later resampling or filter effects require revised sample-domain accounting; implementation is still pending.

noise_model.injection_point: Once at the receiver, after the LOS and any reflected signal paths are combined.

received_eb_n0_to_noise_variance_rule.reference_noise_generation: n_s = sqrt(sigma_s^2/2)*(u + j*v), with independent u,v drawn from N(0,1).

waveform_sample_mapping.condition: Use the agreed square unitary transmit/receive basis transforms on the same discrete sample grid, without additional resampling or filtering gain.
waveform_sample_mapping.note: Unitary receiver basis transforms preserve white complex AWGN covariance. The initial sample grid is 60 MHz without additional oversampling or resampling. Re-derive the sample-domain scaling if later sampling or filtering introduces additional factors; this rule does not select physical filter settings.

received_eb_n0_to_noise_variance_rule.note: Use the agreed data-symbol energy and analytic transform factors on the initial 60 MHz grid. Do not infer noise variance from each random frame's instantaneous measured power. Additional physical filtering remains a separate design decision.

noise_model.basis: A controlled first BER comparison; interference, phase noise, and other real-link impairments are not included in this noise model.

receiver_doppler_compensation.receiver_knowledge: The receiver is given exactly the same snapshot common-Doppler value used by the channel generator, without estimation error.
receiver_doppler_compensation.correction: After channel and receiver AWGN, multiply received samples by exp(-j*2*pi*f_D*n/F_s) to remove the common snapshot frequency shift before waveform-specific demodulation.
receiver_doppler_compensation.note: This entry remains scoped to the single-path baseline. The separately agreed A/B three-path policy is in channel_model.multipath_followup.doppler_effect_followup; imperfect common correction remains unselected.

doppler_comparison.doppler_value_source: Computed, not chosen: -carrier_frequency_hz * slant_range_rate / speed_of_light, with slant-range rate estimated by a 1-second centered difference; Doppler values rounded to 0.1 Hz.
doppler_comparison.baseline_snapshot_interpretation: Keep the original low/high snapshot shifts as orbit-derived inputs. Both have zero residual common Doppler under perfect correction; their BER statistics should coincide at equal received Eb/N0 with other conditions matched. They are not distinct Doppler-stress conditions in the initial baseline.
doppler_comparison.basis: Retain peak elevation and the visible-pass exit at 10 degrees as the original low/high snapshot references. First validate the perfectly common-Doppler-compensated single-path baseline, then compare paired three-path A/B conditions under the separate agreed common-correction policy. Maximum residual Doppler magnitudes and the signed [0,+d,-d] path pattern are agreed; native pilot estimators and their initial search settings are now implemented and initially diagnosed, while data equalization and full BER remain pending. Recompute times and shifts if the draft pass changes.

result_interpretation.comparison_scope: Resource- and energy-budget-matched comparison of four pilot-based transceiver designs, including their native pilot/channel-estimation/equalization effects; this is not a perfect-CSI isolation of intrinsic waveform differences.
result_interpretation.swept_input: Common received data-symbol-referenced E_b/N_0 in dB; use the existing exploratory sweep and noise-normalization rules.
result_interpretation.measured_output: BER, measured as erroneous recovered information bits divided by measured transmitted information bits.
result_interpretation.fixed_eb_n0_comparison: At the same received E_b/N_0 and matched comparison conditions, lower BER indicates better reliability.
result_interpretation.target_ber_comparison: The same measured curves may also compare the E_b/N_0 required to reach a target BER, when the simulated range and statistical uncertainty support that comparison. A target BER is not selected here.
result_interpretation.snr_note: E_b/N_0 is a bit-energy to noise-spectral-density ratio related to waveform SNR, not an interchangeable label for sample-power SNR. BER is the primary measured performance metric; E_b/N_0 is the controlled horizontal axis.

eb_energy_reference.definition: Average normalized data-symbol energy per information bit: Eb = Es/bits_per_symbol for the initial uncoded comparison.
eb_energy_reference.note: Exclusion from Eb accounting does not decide whether pilots or guards are present in the transmitted waveform. Keep the agreed pilot resource/energy fairness policy; evaluate a total-frame-energy-per-information-bit reference separately when overhead is designed.

extension_tracking.interpretation: Index of discussed extensions and reviews, not a new execution order or selection of pending numerical parameters. The main extension_order remains the agreed staging rule; none of these BER extensions has been run.

evaluation.initial_stage_interpretation: Check basic transmitter/receiver behavior and energy/noise normalization against the common uncoded Gray-mapped 16-QAM AWGN reference under ideal processing. Similar BER is expected for matched ideal implementations; no Doppler-robustness ranking is inferred at this stage.

monte_carlo_measurement.counted_bits: Count transmitted information/data bits and their recovered counterparts; exclude known pilot, prefix, guard, and padding content from the BER denominator.
monte_carlo_measurement.framing_note: The 160-frame equivalence assumes all 256*64 grid cells carry uncoded 16-QAM data. Recompute framing when pilots or reserved cells are introduced while preserving the common information-bit quota; this decision does not select their allocation.

pilot_stage_framing_budget.note: Arithmetic for the agreed masks' 12288 data cells with 4 bits per symbol and the unchanged 10485760-bit quota. Final-frame padding/measurement handling remains to be designed; do not round the bit quota or count pilots/guards/padding as measured information bits.

monte_carlo_measurement.budget_basis: An initial approximately ten-million-bit budget gives about 100 expected errors if the true BER is 1e-5. This is a rough precision planning basis, not an error-count stopping target, a guaranteed error count, or a guarantee of precision at lower BER.

reporting.zero_error_interpretation: Record zero observed errors and the measured bit count without asserting that the true BER is exactly zero; report uncertainty using the selected interval method.

eb_n0_refinement.selection_basis: Select the region where BER changes or the four waveforms differ after the exploratory sweep; extend the bounds if needed.

evaluation.eb_n0_sweep_basis: A computationally economical initial scan, not a measured STARLINK-5285 receive SNR range.
